generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: fresh sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: copy from parent pool; NULL share per null_targets when nullable; 10% of parent rows left without children
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: uniform in observed min..max; NULL share per null_targets when nullable
generic_sampling_rules.integer_64: for 64-bit integer columns (events.device_id, events_relevant.device_id, gender_age.device_id, gender_age_train.device_id, gender_age_test.device_id, phone_brand_device_model2.device_id, sample_submission.device_id): draw from a 64-bit-safe range (e.g. uniform in [-2**63, 2**63-1] or a fixed pool of observed literals); never clamp to 32-bit; boundary literals sampled directly from the boundary set plus one step on each side
generic_sampling_rules.text_enum: pick from explicit enum pool; NULL share per null_targets when nullable
generic_sampling_rules.text_free: pick from small pool of observed literals plus case variants; NULL share per null_targets when nullable
generic_sampling_rules.datetime: uniform between 2016-01-01 and 2016-12-31, format '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.0'; NULL share per null_targets when nullable
generic_sampling_rules.real_coord: longitude uniform 0..180, latitude uniform 0..90; NULL share per null_targets when nullable
generic_sampling_rules.boundary: for each listed literal include literal, literal-step, literal+step; for 64-bit integer columns use the integer_64 rule so no 32-bit clamp applies
generic_sampling_rules.near_variant: for each LIKE/equality literal include case variants and prefix/suffix variants
generic_sampling_rules.tie: duplicate the value at the listed rank so ORDER BY has ties
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate_share: 20-50% of rows repeat a value on the DISTINCT column
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: default 5-30% NULL on nullable columns; per-column compact shares in null_targets override this default (e.g. gender_age demographics 0.597, events_relevant.device_id 1.0); at least one NULL row per nullable column

generation_specification.uncertainty: Exact distributions of app_id and device_id are unknown; generation uses fresh sequential keys and copies through foreign keys. Null shares follow the compact statistics: gender_age demographics 0.597, events_relevant.device_id 1.0; these per-column shares override the generic 5-30% null_share rule. events.device_id and events_relevant.device_id are 64-bit integer columns; boundary literals must be sampled without 32-bit clamping. Reproducibility must be verified after fixing the 64-bit sampler; construction separation rate should be re-checked after all units build successfully; preservation of compact rows should be explicitly verified post-write.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 11 of 20 units failed with ValueError('empty range for randrange() (3915082290673129984, 2147483648, -3915082288525646336)'). This is raised in values.py NumberSampler.sample() -> r.randint(int(lo), int(hi)) where lo/hi come from BoundaryNumberSampler for events.device_id / events_relevant.device_id. The boundary values are ~3.9e18 and ~4.07e18, but NumberSampler.__init__ clamps self.max = min(2*10**scale, _MAX) = 2**31-1 = 2147483647, while lo is set to min(boundary)-5 ≈ 3.9e18. So lo > hi and randint raises. The boundary literals for device_id (huge 64-bit values) are incompatible with the 32-bit clamp in NumberSampler.
issues.requested_revision: Fix the sampler so that large integer boundary literals (device_id values ~4e18) do not produce an empty randint range. E.g. in BoundaryNumberSampler / NumberSampler, when lo/hi are supplied, do not clamp hi to _MAX (or clamp lo as well), or use a dedicated sampler for 64-bit integer columns that draws from the boundary set plus a safe range. Ensure all 20 units build without exceptions.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 'reproducible': false. The CLI seeds rng = random.Random(seed_base*100003 + i) per unit, but build_random_instance consumes rng in a data-dependent way and, more importantly, the failure of 11 units means the same seed does not yield the same set of instances across runs. Also, the per-unit rng is created inside _one but the multiprocessing map order and the 'if os.path.exists(p): return skipped' short-circuit make the produced set depend on prior runs. The spec requires reproducible generation.
issues.requested_revision: Make generation deterministic: ensure a fixed seed produces identical instance files regardless of prior state (e.g. do not skip on existing files silently, or document that skipping is idempotent), and confirm reproducibility after fixing the ValueError. Re-run and verify 'reproducible': true.

issues.evidence: Specification 'generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric' says 'uniform in observed min..max', but the per-column boundary targets for events.device_id and events_relevant.device_id are 64-bit values (~3.9e18, ~4.07e18) that are far outside any 32-bit range and are not 'observed min..max' of a typical integer column. The program's NumberSampler clamps to 2**31-1, which conflicts with these boundary values. The specification does not state that these device_id columns are 64-bit or how to sample them.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the specification that events.device_id / events_relevant.device_id are 64-bit integer columns and that boundary literals must be sampled without 32-bit clamping (or provide a dedicated integer-64 rule). This resolves the ambiguity that led to the engineer's ValueError.

issues.evidence: Specification 'null_targets' lists gender_age.gender/age/group and events_relevant.device_id, and the uncertainty note says null shares follow compact statistics (0.597 for gender_age demographics, 1.0 for events_relevant.device_id). Execution feedback shows gender_age.age/gender/group NULL 357/601 (≈0.594, consistent) and events_relevant.device_id NULL 2042/2042 (1.0, consistent). However, the specification's generic rule 'null_share: 5-30% NULL on nullable columns' conflicts with the 0.597 and 1.0 shares. The program uses _NULL_SHARE overrides, which is correct, but the spec text is internally inconsistent.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile the generic 5-30% null_share rule with the per-column compact-share overrides (0.597, 1.0) so the specification is self-consistent. State explicitly that per-column compact shares override the generic 5-30% rule.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 'construction_pairs': {'eligible': 401, 'separated': 75}. Only 75 of 401 eligible pairs are separated. While a missing separation alone does not prove a generation error, the low separation rate combined with the 11 failed units (which never produced instances) means many pairs could not be exercised. After fixing the ValueError, re-check separation.
issues.requested_revision: After fixing the ValueError and reproducibility issues, re-run construction and report the separation rate. If separation remains low, investigate whether boundary/near-variant values are actually being planted (e.g. BoundaryNumberSampler for device_id, EnumSampler boundary inclusion) and whether the compact-row copy dominates the generated rows.

issues.evidence: writer.py copies the compact database (shutil.copyfile) and appends generated rows. Execution feedback shows rows_added for all tables and integrity fk_violations=0, not_null_violations=0, pk_duplicates=0, not_ok=0, which is good. However, the 'preservation of compact rows' is only implicitly verified. The spec says compact rows are never deleted or changed; the program does not explicitly verify this after writing.
issues.requested_revision: Add an explicit post-write check (or report) that the compact rows are preserved unchanged (e.g. compare row counts and a checksum of compact rows before/after). This is a verification gap, not a blocking error, but should be confirmed.

unresolved_checks: Reproducibility could not be confirmed because 11 units failed; must be re-verified after the ValueError fix.
Construction separation rate (75/401) is low; needs re-evaluation after all units build successfully.
Preservation of compact rows is not explicitly verified by the program; only inferred from integrity checks.

issues.evidence: Specification's generic_sampling_rules.datetime says 'uniform between 2016-01-01 and 2016-12-31', but the per_column_exceptions for events.timestamp require boundary literals 2015-12-31, 2016-01-01, 2016-12-31, 2017-01-01 and near variants 2016-05-03..05. The program (values.py DateTimeSampler) draws uniformly in [2016-01-01, 2016-12-31 23:59:59] and only includes boundary/near literals via the element pool with probability p (0.0 or 0.2). With p=0.0 the boundary literals are never emitted, so the comparison_boundary and like_near_variant targets for events.timestamp are not guaranteed. This is a soft coverage gap, not an integrity error.
issues.requested_revision: Either state explicitly that boundary/near literals for events.timestamp are only sampled with the element-pool probability (and accept that some instances may not contain them), or require the sampler to always include the boundary set (e.g. force p>0 for columns with boundary targets).

issues.evidence: values.py Int64Sampler._draw only draws boundary+step values (lo=min(boundary)-2, hi=max(boundary)+2) and never uses the observed pool range or a wide 64-bit range. The specification's integer_64 rule says 'draw from a 64-bit-safe range (e.g. uniform in [-2**63, 2**63-1] or a fixed pool of observed literals)'. The implementation is a fixed pool of boundary literals plus small steps, which is acceptable per the 'or a fixed pool' clause, but the observed pool is only used with probability p. This is consistent with the spec's alternative, so not a blocking error.
issues.requested_revision: No change required; optionally document that the fixed boundary pool is the chosen 64-bit strategy.

issues.evidence: instance.py fill_foreign_keys_consistently sets nullable FK null_share from _NULL_SHARE with default 0.10, but for events_relevant.device_id the spec sets 1.0 (all NULL). Execution feedback confirms 'events_relevant.device_id: generated rows: NULL 2697 / 2697'. This matches the spec's per-column override. However, the spec's generic rule also says 'at least one NULL row per nullable column' and 'rows with non-NULL values' for every nullable column; for events_relevant.device_id the spec explicitly overrides to 1.0, so all-NULL is intended. Consistent.

instance.py _plant_nulls is applied to non-FK columns only (FK columns handled in fill_foreign_keys_consistently). For gender_age demographics the spec sets null_share 0.597; execution shows 778/1303 ≈ 0.597. Consistent. For gender_age_train demographics the spec does not override, so default 0.10 applies; execution shows 140/1385 ≈ 0.101. Consistent.

writer.py copies the compact DB (shutil.copyfile) then appends rows; compact_sha256 is reported and n_skipped_existing=0, reproducible=true, integrity fk_violations=0, not_null_violations=0, pk_duplicates=0. Compact rows are preserved by construction (copy + append, no deletes/updates).

Construction separation: 92/401 eligible pairs separated, 0 unknown executions. This is a partial separation, which is expected for a random generator; the instructions state a missing separation alone does not establish a generation error. No blocking issue.
issues.requested_revision: No change required; note that separation rate is moderate and could be improved by strengthening boundary/near-variant emission (see first issue).

issues.evidence: Specification semantic_rules_and_formulas for app_events.is_installed says 'is_installed IN (0,1)' and is_active 'IN (0,1)', but per_column_exceptions comparison_boundary targets include values [-1,0,1,2] for is_active and [0,1,2] for is_installed. The program (values.py BOUNDARY) uses these boundary sets, so generated rows can contain -1 and 2, violating the stated semantic formula. Execution integrity checks did not flag this (no CHECK constraint), but it is an internal inconsistency between the semantic rule and the boundary targets.
issues.requested_revision: Reconcile: either relax the semantic formula to allow the boundary values (e.g. 'is_installed IN (0,1,2)' / 'is_active IN (-1,0,1,2)') or remove -1/2 from the boundary targets. Since the boundary targets are derived from observed query literals (comparison_boundary), the formula should be widened to match.

issues.evidence: Specification semantic_rules_and_formulas for gender_age.gender says "gender IS NULL OR gender IN ('M','F')", but per_column_exceptions comparison_boundary targets include 'f' and 'm' (lowercase). The program EnumSampler includes boundary values, so lowercase 'f'/'m' can be generated, violating the stated formula. Same for gender_age.group (formula lists only canonical 12 values, but boundary targets include 'f23-', 'f27-28', 'm27-28').
issues.requested_revision: Widen the semantic formulas to include the case variants used as boundary targets, or drop the case variants from boundary targets. The boundary targets come from observed query literals, so the formulas should be relaxed to 'gender IN (M,F,m,f)' etc.

issues.evidence: Specification semantic_rules_and_formulas for phone_brand_device_model2.phone_brand and device_model and label_categories.category do not constrain values, but boundary targets include case variants and near variants (e.g. '中兴x', 'm8 ey', 'home decoration'). These are consistent with text_free sampling; no formula conflict. However, label_categories.category near variants include empty string '' and ' x', which are not covered by any formula — acceptable since no formula constrains category.

values.py build_spec_sampler for text columns with boundary/near variants uses StringSampler with els including boundary and case/str variants, but StringSampler.sample() with probability p draws random strings from CHARSET, which can produce values outside the enum (e.g. for gender/group the EnumSampler is used instead, so OK; for phone_brand/device_model/category the EnumSampler is used via _enum_pool_for, so OK). For columns with boundary but no enum (none in this schema besides those covered), StringSampler would emit arbitrary strings. In this schema all text columns with boundary targets are covered by enum pools, so no violation observed.
issues.requested_revision: No change required for this schema; note that StringSampler fallback could violate enum formulas if a future column has boundary targets but no enum pool.

issues.evidence: instance.py sample_fresh_primary_keys drops rows whose PK tuple repeats or collides with compact PK. For composite PKs (app_events, app_events_relevant) the PK includes event_id and app_id; event_id is an FK drawn from parent pool, app_id from parent pool, so duplicates are possible and dropped. Execution shows pk_duplicates=0. Consistent.

instance.py _fresh_int_keys uses compact_max_int + 1 for single-column integer PKs (app_all.app_id, events.event_id, events_relevant.event_id, label_categories.label_id). But events.event_id and events_relevant.event_id also have comparison_boundary targets [1,2,3,5,6,7] and [1,2,3,154,155,156]. Since _fresh_int_keys overwrites the PK column after sampling, the boundary values for event_id are never emitted for events/events_relevant PKs. The boundary targets for events.event_id and events_relevant.event_id are therefore not satisfied by the PK column. (app_events.event_id is an FK, not PK-only, so boundary values can appear there.)
issues.requested_revision: Either (a) allow the PK sampler to include boundary literals for event_id (e.g. start fresh keys above compact max but also inject boundary values as separate rows), or (b) acknowledge that boundary targets for events.event_id/events_relevant.event_id are only reachable via FK columns (app_events.event_id, app_events_relevant.event_id) and adjust the spec's per_column_exceptions accordingly. This is a coverage gap, not an integrity error.
